top.title: AI-powered cyber threats are changing the rules of enterprise recovery
top.description: Cybersecurity has long been a contest between attackers finding new ways in and defenders trying to keep them out. Artificial intelligence is making that contest more complicated, giving cybercriminals new ways to develop and adapt their attacks while putting additional pressure on conventional cyber defences. For enterprise IT leaders, the challenge extends beyond preventing a breach. What happens when an attacker gets through? Can compromised data be identified, clean copies recovered, and essential systems brought back online without prolonged disruption? These questions are becoming increasingly important as organizations confront both traditional threats and emerging AI-powered cyberattacks. A successful defense strategy must, therefore, account for what happens after an incident, not just the measures designed to prevent one. Making recovery part of the defence This is where cyber-resilient enterprise storage has an important role to play. Rather than relying solely on traditional backup processes, organizations need ways to protect critical data, detect potential compromise, establish which copies can safely be recovered, and restore those copies as quickly as possible. Infinidat addresses this challenge through its InfiniBox and InfiniBox SSA enterprise storage platforms, which incorporate the company’s InfiniSafe cyber resilience and recovery software suite. InfiniSafe combines immutable snapshots, which cannot be altered or deleted during their protected retention period, with logical air-gapping to isolate the management plane from the data plane. Fenced forensic environments provide a separate space for validating data before recovery. The technology also supports automated cyber protection, allowing security monitoring data center wide cyber security software applications or a Security Operations Center (SOC) to automatically talk to InfiniBoxes and trigger immutable snapshots when suspicious activity is detected. This helps reduce the window in which critical data might be exposed. For organizations concerned about recovering compromised information, optional InfiniSafe Cyber Detection uses AI-based analysis to help identify cyber affected data and locate the last known good copy of the data for recovery. Speed is another consideration. Infinidat guarantees recovery of immutable snapshots in one minute or less for InfiniBox and InfiniBox SSA, subject to the guarantee’s terms and conditions. Ultimately, cyber resilience isn’t about assuming every cyberattack can be stopped. It’s about ensuring that when defences are breached, organizations have the tools and processes to recover trusted data and limit the operational consequences. For enterprise IT teams, that makes recovery readiness an essential part of the cybersecurity conversation. Sponsored by Infinidat

top.title: Supernova explodes before astronomers' eyes | Space photo of the day for Nov. 18, 2026
top.description: null Before-and-after photos showing the appearance of a new supernova designated SN 2026ahvu. (Image credit: Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Acknowledgment: PIs: G. Narayan & T. Murphey (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign) Image processing: M. Zamani & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)) A new supernova has been spotted exploding in the spiral galaxy NGC 1433, about 50 million light-years from Earth. What is it? Researchers have discovered a new supernova called SN 2026ahvu. A Type Ia supernova, this event took place in a system with two stars orbiting one another (also known as a binary system), in which typically one star is an exploding white dwarf . During most type Ia supernovae, the white dwarf pulls material away from the other star until enough accumulates on its surface to create an explosion. Finding galaxies where stellar explosions are taking place isn't a rarity. However, this supernova is unique in how early it was captured. If the supernova were starting to dim, researchers might infer that the event was ending. However, according to details shared when it was first spotted, as well as later observations, this supernova was discovered while getting brighter. This indicates that the supernova was likely caught early in the process of exploding, providing researchers with a unique opportunity to observe the event as it is taking place. By exploring observations of the galaxy before, during and (in the future) after the supernova event, researchers can investigate this type Ia supernova and how it affected the system in which it took place. Why is it incredible? Scientists made this discovery using ATLAS, or the Asteroid Terrestrial-impact System, which is a robotic astronomical survey made up of telescopes across both hemispheres. ATLAS is designed to spot incoming near-Earth objects like asteroids before they can reach Earth. It's essentially an asteroid impact early warning system. But just because that's what the system is designed for doesn't mean that's all it can do. The system can also spot other objects moving through space and, in this instance, it was able to capture observations of this supernova. Following its initial discovery, other observations of the supernova were made using NOIRLab's Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and Gemini South telescope.

top.title: Space robot legend Voyager 1 is now more than 1 light-day away
top.description: NASA's Voyager 1 probe is now more than one light-day from Earth – so distant that a radio signal takes 24 hours to reach it. The veteran spacecraft has spent almost 50 years getting there. Voyager 1 was launched on September 5, 1977, from Cape Canaveral in Florida. Planning for the mission began in the 1960s, while NASA was working feverishly to put a man on the Moon ahead of the Soviet Union. A rare alignment of the outer planets made a tour of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune possible. Voyager 2 eventually visited all four; Voyager 1's route prioritized Saturn's moon Titan, ruling out a subsequent encounter with Pluto. Voyager 1 completed a flyby of Jupiter in 1979, and passed Saturn and Titan in 1980. Its final imaging sequence in 1990 produced the solar system "Family Portrait," including the famous Pale Blue Dot image of Earth. The cameras were then switched off for good. Thirty-six years after those final pictures, Voyager 1 remains in contact with Earth, with two science instruments still operating: the magnetometer and plasma wave subsystem. Others have been shut down over the decades to conserve the dwindling power supplied by its radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs). Dr Garry Hunt, a member of Voyager's original imaging team, told The Register : "Voyager's real success is the way it used reliable equipment. Well-tested Mariner equipment, and special new things that had come about for it. "We had fault protection on board as well. If anything goes wrong, it automatically switches to a backup. So there was always a backup. There was always a safe mode. We had to have radiation protection on board … when we designed this, we didn't really know the magnetic environment around Jupiter, and to be told it was so strong, 1,000 times stronger than we anticipated, really threw everything up in the air, and so that had to be dealt with." Hunt paid tribute to the succession of project managers and engineers who have kept the probe running over the years. "I think this was a really wonderful example of project management, of clever management of engineering, and interesting science coming out of it, which has made history books and gone to be a catalyst for other things in the future," he said. Voyager 1 may now take two days to answer a call from Earth. After almost 50 years, the remarkable thing is that it still answers at all. ®

top.title: Gaming Phenomenon ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Goes Live After 13-Year Wait
top.description: After 13 years of waiting, including two delays and several leaks, the first gamers began playing Wednesday the latest instalment of “Grand Theft Auto”, the most expensive — and among the most profitable — video game ever developed. “GTA VI” becomes available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles at midnight Thursday in each region where it will be available. That meant it launched first in New Zealand (at 1100 GMT on Wednesday), with many players around the world changing their console location settings to the far-eastern country to be among the first to enter the new Vice City. “I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time that the anticipation for this is crazy,” Australian student Riley Fennel told AFP ahead of the launch. Although Rockstar Games, the studio behind GTA, has not yet released advance unit sales figures, specialist firm Sensor Tower estimates they have already surpassed 15 million. That would be more than $1.5 billion in revenue before the game even came out, for a budget estimated at $1 billion to $1.5 billion, which would be unprecedented. According to the British analytics firm Omdia, sales of “GTA VI” could reach $3.2 billion by the end of the year. An organiser fixes a poster of the video game ‘Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI’ ahead of its launch party in Chennai on November 17, 2026. Photo by R.SATISH BABU / AFP ‘Taylor Swift of games’ “No other concert or box office release has ever generated that much capital. And so that makes it one of the outliers in entertainment,” said Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business. “This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” the industry specialist said. Rockstar’s parent company, US publisher Take-Two Interactive, has rolled out a massive marketing campaign to establish the title as a mass cultural product that transcends the boundaries of video games. “The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said James McWhirter at Omdia. “I’m going to take four days off,” said Dmytro Shkambara, a 27-year-old Ukrainian player living in Berlin, who said he had been planning this first game session “for a very long time”. Like him, many fans have already booked time off to immerse themselves in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida. The human resources platform Remote said it had seen a 32 percent increase in leave requests around the world for November 19. Touted as bigger, better and more realistic than its predecessors, “GTA VI” follows the adventures of a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style couple trying to survive in the Miami-inspired, crime-ravaged Vice City. Since its beginnings, the series has won players over with its increasingly realistic reconstructions of fictionalised cities and the great freedom of action offered in a highly detailed open world. top.title: New York State Pension Fund Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake by More Than 10%
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York State Pension Fund Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake by More Than 10% The New York State Common Retirement Fund raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by more than 10% in the third quarter, to 352,850 shares worth $54.0 million at Sept. 30. The pension fund disclosed the position in a Form 13F filed Tuesday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. It added 33,000 shares from the 319,850 it reported at June 30. That is an increase of a little more than 10%. The filing does not say why the pension fund added the shares. The reported value nearly doubled, to $54.0 million from $27.8 million. Strategy’s stock closed the quarter at $153.09, up from $86.93 at midyear, so most of the gain in dollar value came from the rally, not from the added shares. A small slice of a large pension fund The fund is one of the largest public pension plans in the U.S. It holds the assets used to pay retirement benefits for New York’s state and local public employees. Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli, the fund’s trustee, valued it at an estimated $309.7 billion as of June 30, the latest official figure. There is not yet a published valuation for Sept. 30. Public equities are only part of the portfolio. As of March 31, they accounted for 39.4% of the fund’s assets, with the rest in cash and bonds, private equity, real estate and other alternatives. The 13F lists 2,975 holdings worth $71.3 billion. The Strategy stake is a small slice of that book, less than a tenth of a percent. Strategy has made bitcoin its primary treasury asset. The company held 850,849 bitcoin as of Nov. 15, with an aggregate purchase price of $64.20 billion, or $75,452 a coin. Institutional managers have 45 days after quarter-end to file a 13F. Tuesday’s report is the first official look at the pension fund’s third-quarter buying, after the stock had already fallen sharply from the $153.09 price used in the filing. Strategy shares have already fallen Strategy closed Tuesday at $96.50, below $100 and about 37% under its Sept. 30 close. At that price, the same 352,850 shares are worth about $34 million, roughly $20 million less than the value in the filing. The common shares also finished under Strategy’s STRC preferred stock, which closed at $98.70. That is the first time they have closed below the preferred since mid-August. The stock is down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close of $121.07. A 13F is a snapshot. It does not show whether the pension fund bought or sold shares in October or November, when most of that decline took place. Coinbase and miners, but no bitcoin ETFs The information table lists no shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust or other spot bitcoin ETFs, and no shares of Strategy’s preferred stock. The pension fund does hold Coinbase (COIN). It reported 109,433 shares at Sept. 30, a little below the 111,633 shares it held at midyear. The reported value still rose, to $20.4 million from $16.3 million, as Coinbase’s stock climbed. It also holds a string of bitcoin miners.

top.title: StubHub International warns customer data may have left the venue
top.description: Ticket resale giant StubHub International has warned customers that a recent breach may have exposed their personal information to cybercriminals. The company said it detected "unauthorized access to certain systems" on its platform between late October and early November. Customer notification emails seen by The Register list potentially affected information including names, email addresses, phone numbers, and country or regional settings. StubHub International, operated by Ticketbis S.L., apologized for the intrusion and offered the usual promise to implement security enhancements after the fact. The company said it had addressed "certain vulnerabilities" while containing the incident and was continuing to monitor for suspicious activity. Outside cybersecurity experts are assisting with the ongoing investigation. The company warned that any exposed information could be used to make subsequent scams more convincing. "To date, we have found no evidence of unauthorised access to account passwords , banking information or payment card details," the email stated. "We also have no evidence that the compromised information has been used fraudulently. "However, there is a risk that third parties could use this information to attempt fraud, identity theft or phishing through emails, messages or calls that appear to come from StubHub International or other trusted organizations." The Register contacted StubHub International for more information, such as how many customers were affected, but it did not respond. Digital Fuel Capital bought StubHub International from Viagogo in 2021 after the UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) required the international business to be sold to address competition concerns. In June, the CMA fined Ticketbis £889,200 and ordered refunds exceeding £590,000 after finding that mandatory fees were omitted from upfront ticket prices. StubHub International also recently faced criticism for allowing a single ticket tout to advertise £1 million worth of U2 tickets, despite its stated opposition to ticket-buying bots. ®

nigeria.description: The Senate has urged the Federal Government to expedite action on the implementation of the recommendations of its investigative committee on the death of 37 young artisanal miners in the custody of Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Niger Command. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the resolution followed the consideration of a motion sponsored by Sen. Sani Musa (APC-Niger East) over the death of the miners on Sept. 17 in Minna, Niger. The senate called for appropriate sanctions against the officers found culpable and institutional reforms within NSCDC to prevent a recurrence of the incident. It also resolved to constitute a delegation to pay a condolence visit to the bereaved families. The lawmakers further directed the Committees on Interior, Solid Minerals, Human Rights, Police Affairs and Judiciary to monitor implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations and report progress to the senate. Presenting the motion, Musa said the deceased were arrested during operations against suspected illegal mining activities but subsequently died under circumstances that raised concerns about their conditions of detention and protection of fundamental human rights. He said that the federal government had established a 10-member independent investigative committee, chaired by Mr Jonathan Kure, to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths, determine responsibility and recommend appropriate measures. Musa noted that the committee had submitted its report, identifying lapses and recommending sanctions, institutional reforms and financial compensation for the families of the deceased. Seconding the motion, Sen. Ned Nwoko (APC-Delta North) described the incident as a national tragedy but called for an objective examination of the circumstances surrounding the deaths. “It is a national tragedy when so many young lives are lost under circumstances such as the ones we are discussing,” Nwoko said. nigeria.title: State Police: Senate Directs NASS Clerk To Transmit Amendment Bill To Tinubu For Assent
nigeria.description: The Senate has directed the clerk to the National Assembly to transmit the Constitution alteration bill providing for the establishment of State Police to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The upper chamber has also asked the Executive to forward the National Policing Bill to the National Assembly for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage to establish the operational framework for subnational policing. The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, during plenary today. Policemen at the Niger State Police Command (Photo by Abdullahi Egba/Channels TV) In its deliberations, Senator Bamidele recalled that the National Assembly had processed an executive bill seeking to amend the 1999 Constitution to establish state police as part of Nigeria’s national policing structure. He noted that both chambers overwhelmingly approved the proposed amendment, with the Senate passing the bill on June 24, 2026, and the House of Representatives following suit on July 23, 2026, securing the constitutionally required two-thirds majority. The bill was subsequently transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly for approval in line with Section 9(2) of the Constitution. The Senate Leader noted that the Senate confirmed that all 36 state legislatures had now endorsed the proposed amendment and transmitted their resolutions to the National Assembly. Having satisfied the constitutional requirements under Sections 9(1) and 9(2), the Senate maintained that the amendment had fulfilled the conditions necessary for its passage. The upper chamber therefore urged the Executive to submit the National Policing Bill to provide the legal and operational framework for the implementation of State Police. The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, announced on Monday that all 36 State Houses of Assembly had approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police, clearing the way for the bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The clerk described it as 100 per cent approval by the state legislatures, as the approval exceeded the constitutional requirement of at least 24 state assemblies under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. “The Clerk to the National Assembly wishes to announce that all the thirty-six (36) State Houses of Assembly have approved ‘A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for related Matters’. “This represents one hundred percent (100%) endorsement by the State Houses of Assembly, which exceeds the threshold of twenty-four (24), provided under Section 9(2) of the Constitution (as amended),” Ogunlana had stated. The development marked the completion of the state assemblies’ consideration of the proposed amendment, following weeks of legislative engagement over the establishment of state police. nigeria.title: 2027: My US congressional meetings not for endorsement — Obi
nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has clarified that his recent meetings with members of the United States Congress in Washington, DC, were not intended to secure endorsements for his political ambition. Obi, who made the clarification in a statement posted on his Facebook page, said reports suggesting that his engagements with American lawmakers amounted to endorsements of his political aspirations were inaccurate. He explained that the visit was primarily aimed at engaging congressional leaders and other influential American stakeholders on issues concerning Nigeria’s development, citizens’ welfare and the consolidation of democracy. The post read; “I wish to address the inaccurate interpretation presented in certain media reports concerning my recent engagements with members of the United States Congress in Washington, DC. “As I expressly noted in my remarks, my visit to the United States was not intended to secure an endorsement, and I did not characterise my meetings as endorsements of my political aspirations by the US Congress or any of its members. “The primary purpose of the visit was to engage with congressional leaders and other influential American stakeholders, exchange perspectives, and discuss matters related to Nigeria’s development, the welfare of our citizens and, most importantly, the consolidation of our democracy. “I am especially concerned with strengthening democratic institutions, advancing accountability, and ensuring that Nigeria’s electoral process produces elections that are free, fair, transparent and credible. nigeria.title: Putin-Trump-Xi: Three men, three different agendas
nigeria.description: An unprecedented trilateral summit of the leaders of China, Russia and the US will provide startling images and unsettle Europe this week, but all three presidents are approaching the meeting with starkly different agendas. Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will meet Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen for talks that have echoes of the US-UK-USSR February 1945 “big three” summit in Yalta. At that meeting, which took place months before the end of World War II, the leaders of Britain, the Soviet Union and the US agreed the postwar division of Europe. Europe, which will not have a representative at Thursday’s talks, will be eyeing them warily. The smiles and friendly handshakes may also cause chills in Ukraine, after almost half a decade of war with Russia, and Taiwan, the democratic island viewed by China as part of its territory. But analysts say it is unlikely that the meeting will result in a landmark breakthrough on key issues such as Ukraine, nuclear disarmament and AI, even if the fact it is taking place at all is remarkable. Here AFP looks at what the three men will want from the meeting. Putin: imagery and Ukraine On paper, Putin will be in the meeting as the junior partner, presiding over a country whose population, let alone economy, is dwarfed by both the United States and China. But the war sparked by Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine, which Trump famously vowed to resolve in 24 hours, will be at the centre of the talks as the conflict grinds towards its fifth anniversary. Putin will be buoyed by being able to set out his conditions for ending the war without Kyiv’s chief allies, the Europeans, or Ukraine being at the table. “He wants Russia, the US and China to decide everyone else’s geopolitical fate. But in the end it’s impossible to decide on the fundamentals of European security without Europeans,” said Fredrik Wesslau, senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR). The optics of the meeting, set to be relayed extensively by Russia’s state-controlled media, are also very important for Putin who has always pressed for Moscow to be seen as a great global power even after the collapse of the USSR. “A seat alongside the American and Chinese presidents would affirm Russia’s status as a global power, despite its much weaker economic position,” said Tsiporah Fried, senior fellow at the Hudson Institute. “Political rehabilitation would be a gain even without concessions on territory, sanctions, or Ukraine’s future alignment,” she added. Trump: nuclear and overcoming midterms Trump and the White House have framed the trilateral summit as a way of advancing nuclear arms control, although the president himself admitted before leaving Washington “it’s a tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes.” The imagery is also important for Trump as the 80-year-old contemplates his last two years in office as a lame-duck president followin

business.title: New York State Pension Fund Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake by More Than 10%
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York State Pension Fund Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake by More Than 10% The New York State Common Retirement Fund raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by more than 10% in the third quarter, to 352,850 shares worth $54.0 million at Sept. 30. The pension fund disclosed the position in a Form 13F filed Tuesday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. It added 33,000 shares from the 319,850 it reported at June 30. That is an increase of a little more than 10%. The filing does not say why the pension fund added the shares. The reported value nearly doubled, to $54.0 million from $27.8 million. Strategy’s stock closed the quarter at $153.09, up from $86.93 at midyear, so most of the gain in dollar value came from the rally, not from the added shares. A small slice of a large pension fund The fund is one of the largest public pension plans in the U.S. It holds the assets used to pay retirement benefits for New York’s state and local public employees. Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli, the fund’s trustee, valued it at an estimated $309.7 billion as of June 30, the latest official figure. There is not yet a published valuation for Sept. 30. Public equities are only part of the portfolio. As of March 31, they accounted for 39.4% of the fund’s assets, with the rest in cash and bonds, private equity, real estate and other alternatives. The 13F lists 2,975 holdings worth $71.3 billion. The Strategy stake is a small slice of that book, less than a tenth of a percent. Strategy has made bitcoin its primary treasury asset. The company held 850,849 bitcoin as of Nov. 15, with an aggregate purchase price of $64.20 billion, or $75,452 a coin. Institutional managers have 45 days after quarter-end to file a 13F. Tuesday’s report is the first official look at the pension fund’s third-quarter buying, after the stock had already fallen sharply from the $153.09 price used in the filing. Strategy shares have already fallen Strategy closed Tuesday at $96.50, below $100 and about 37% under its Sept. 30 close. At that price, the same 352,850 shares are worth about $34 million, roughly $20 million less than the value in the filing. The common shares also finished under Strategy’s STRC preferred stock, which closed at $98.70. That is the first time they have closed below the preferred since mid-August. The stock is down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close of $121.07. A 13F is a snapshot. It does not show whether the pension fund bought or sold shares in October or November, when most of that decline took place. Coinbase and miners, but no bitcoin ETFs The information table lists no shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust or other spot bitcoin ETFs, and no shares of Strategy’s preferred stock. The pension fund does hold Coinbase (COIN). It reported 109,433 shares at Sept. 30, a little below the 111,633 shares it held at midyear. The reported value still rose, to $20.4 million from $16.3 million, as Coinbase’s stock climbed. It also holds a string of bitcoin miners.

The bitcoin price had slipped below $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon. It climbed back to about $65,000 that evening after Nvidia beat earnings estimates, then faded through the U.S. morning. The bitcoin price is down about 21% from a month ago, when it traded above $81,000. Waller floats a half-point hike Waller told CNBC in a live interview that the Fed probably needs a half-point increase at its Dec. 8-9 meeting. He said the central bank should reverse its three quarter-point cuts from last year and may need to do more. “You might need to, like, shock people,” Waller said. “I’m very, very concerned about inflation. It’s kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out,” he said. Waller said the Fed should deliver the larger move if it is not prepared to signal a faster pace of hikes in the coming months. He also said about 70% of items in the core services basket are running above 3%, which has nothing to do with oil. The 2-year Treasury yield rose more than 4 basis points to 4.83% after his comments. The dollar hit a 19-month high, and gold dropped 2.5% to its lowest level in more than a year. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says South Korea’s Financial Services Commission plans to publish guidelines next week that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms buy bitcoin and other crypto for investment, a local news agency reported Wednesday. The guidelines will be released alongside the government’s draft of the Digital Asset Basic Act, the country’s planned framework for the crypto industry, according to the report . The FSC plans to convene its Virtual Asset Committee to coincide with the release. The FSC itself has not publicly announced a date for either release. If it lands next week, the move would come one year and nine months after the regulator laid out its roadmap for corporate crypto access in February 2025. A roadmap that stalled That plan opened the market in stages, with nonprofits and crypto service providers coming first, and only to sell. Since June 2025, Korean nonprofits have been able to cash out crypto they receive as donations, and World Vision made the first such trade, selling donated ether on Upbit. Exchanges have also been allowed to sell their own holdings to cover operating costs. Coinone and DigitalX, formerly Korbit, have done so several times after filing disclosures. The second stage, which lets listed companies and firms registered as professional investors trade crypto for investment, was slated for the second half of 2025. It never arrived. The holdup is market plumbing. Corporate orders are large, and even Korea’s biggest exchanges have limited room to absorb them without moving prices. “If companies come into the market and trade 5 billion won each, even an exchange like Upbit would struggle to take that volume,” an unnamed industry official told News1. Large trades would normally run through over-the-counter desks, and Korea does not yet have rules governing how those desks operate. What the Basic Act adds The Digital Asset Basic Act is meant to close that gap. It would split crypto service providers into separate business types and set entry and conduct rules for OTC desks, brokers and other operators, the report said. The government’s draft is expected to go to the National Assembly next week. Lawmakers want it passed quickly. The Assembly’s Political Affairs Committee aims to process the bill by January, timed to the implementation of the U.S. GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law. Rep. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram If you have ever wondered what triple digits look like on music’s biggest stage, Beyoncé just gave everyone the answer. The Houston-born global music superstar has officially become the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations, hitting the milestone with her latest nod for “ Morning Dew ( Donk )”, which is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards (2027 Grammys). Released in July 2026 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B’Day, “Morning Dew (Donk)” puts her in a category alongside Kehlani , Victoria Monét , Jill Scott , and Nigerian star Tems . To put the 100-nomination milestone into perspective, no other recording artist has ever crossed into triple digits since the Grammys began. Beyoncé had previously been tied with her husband, Jay-Z , at 88 nominations each before breaking that tie in 2024 with 11 nods for Cowboy Carter to reach 99—and this latest recognition pushes her even further ahead as the artist with the highest number of Grammy nominations in history. Beyoncé holding her three Grammy trophies at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in 2025. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram It is also a good reminder of how long she has been doing this at the highest level. Beyoncé’s Grammy journey started all the way back in 2000 as part of Destiny’s Child with “Bills, Bills, Bills”, and across more than two decades as a solo artist, group member, and collaborator, she has built a record that keeps stretching further ahead of the pack. Alongside holding the title for the most Grammy nominations of all time, she is already the most awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins, a record she first broke in 2023 when she surpassed late conductor Georg Solti ’s 31 trophies. She pushed that tally even higher at the 2025 Grammys, taking home three awards—Album of the Year and Best Country Album for Cowboy Carter, as well as Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” alongside Miley Cyrus . Now all eyes turn to Sunday, 7 February 2027, when the 2027 Grammy Awards take place at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and we find out whether nomination number 100 turns into Grammy win number 36. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. entertainment.description: Sade Adu in the Performer category and Fela Kuti in the Early Influence category, both inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Class of 2026. Nigerian music history just added another major chapter in Los Angeles, and the celebration has been loud from Lagos to London. On Saturday, 14 November 2026, Afrobeat pioneer Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti and Nigerian-British singer Sade Adu were officially inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame during a star-studded ceremony at the Peacock Theatre. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. It also caps off an extraordinary 2026 for his legacy, coming just months after the Recording Academy presented him with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in February, another first for an African artist. Speaking on the milestone, the family reflected on how remarkable it is to see Fela receive both the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and a Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction in the very same year. Meanwhile, Sade Adu —born Helen Folasade Adu in Ibadan—was inducted in th e Performer category as the frontwoman of her acclaimed British band Sade , alongside longtime bandmates Stuart Matthewman , Paul Spencer Denman , and Andrew Hale . Earning their spot on their second nomination, the group behind timeless soul-jazz records such as “Smooth Operator”, “The Sweetest Taboo”, and “Your Love Is King” opted to sit out the ceremony in true low-key fashion, though they shared a warm message thanking fans and dedicating the milestone to their late longtime producer Mike Pela . entertainment.description: Tems receiving the Best African Music Performance at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. entertainment.title: Tems Is Officially a 12-Time Grammy Nominee!
entertainment.description: Tems is officially a 12-time Grammy nominee after securing four nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards. Photo Credit: Tems/Instagram One, two, three… and now 12! Tems has added four more Grammy nominations to her record, bringing her career total to 12 ahead of the 69th Grammy Awards. The latest recognition also makes her the first Nigerian female artist to receive four nominations in a single Grammy year, with this year’s shortlist recognising her work across four categories. The Nigerian singer is in contention for Best Global Music Album with her 10-track EP, Love Is a Kingdom , and Best African Music Performance for “ Big Daddy ”. She has also earned nominations for Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song for “ What You Need ”. The four nominations give her one of the most extensive Nigerian representations at this year’s ceremony and bring her Grammy wins to two, following previous victories in 2023 and 2025. Her relationship with the Recording Academy began in 2022, when she received her first nomination for her contribution to Wizkid ‘s “ Essence ”, which was nominated for Best Global Music Performance at the 64th Grammy Awards. The following year brought three more nominations, this time for her work on Future’s “ Wait for U ” featuring Drake and Beyoncé ‘s Renaissance . She won her first Grammy that night, taking home Best Melodic Rap Performance for “Wait for U”, while also receiving nominations for Album of the Year and Best Rap Song. Tems earned another nomination at the 66th Grammy Awards in 2024 for “ Lift Me Up ”, her contribution to the Black Panther : Wakanda Forever soundtrack, in the Best Song Written for Visual Media category. She returned to the Grammys the following year with three nominations, including Best Global Music Album for her debut album, Born in the Wild , and Best R&B Song for “ Burning ”. Her second Grammy win came in the Best African Music Performance category, where “ Love Me JeJe ” took home the award at the 67th Grammy Awards in February 2025. Now, with four nominations for the 69th edition, Tems has added another significant chapter to her Grammy record. technology.title: AI-powered cyber threats are changing the rules of enterprise recovery
technology.description: Cybersecurity has long been a contest between attackers finding new ways in and defenders trying to keep them out. Artificial intelligence is making that contest more complicated, giving cybercriminals new ways to develop and adapt their attacks while putting additional pressure on conventional cyber defences. For enterprise IT leaders, the challenge extends beyond preventing a breach. What happens when an attacker gets through? Can compromised data be identified, clean copies recovered, and essential systems brought back online without prolonged disruption? These questions are becoming increasingly important as organizations confront both traditional threats and emerging AI-powered cyberattacks. A successful defense strategy must, therefore, account for what happens after an incident, not just the measures designed to prevent one. Making recovery part of the defence This is where cyber-resilient enterprise storage has an important role to play. Rather than relying solely on traditional backup processes, organizations need ways to protect critical data, detect potential compromise, establish which copies can safely be recovered, and restore those copies as quickly as possible. Infinidat addresses this challenge through its InfiniBox and InfiniBox SSA enterprise storage platforms, which incorporate the company’s InfiniSafe cyber resilience and recovery software suite. InfiniSafe combines immutable snapshots, which cannot be altered or deleted during their protected retention period, with logical air-gapping to isolate the management plane from the data plane. Fenced forensic environments provide a separate space for validating data before recovery. The technology also supports automated cyber protection, allowing security monitoring data center wide cyber security software applications or a Security Operations Center (SOC) to automatically talk to InfiniBoxes and trigger immutable snapshots when suspicious activity is detected. This helps reduce the window in which critical data might be exposed. For organizations concerned about recovering compromised information, optional InfiniSafe Cyber Detection uses AI-based analysis to help identify cyber affected data and locate the last known good copy of the data for recovery. Speed is another consideration. Infinidat guarantees recovery of immutable snapshots in one minute or less for InfiniBox and InfiniBox SSA, subject to the guarantee’s terms and conditions. Ultimately, cyber resilience isn’t about assuming every cyberattack can be stopped. It’s about ensuring that when defences are breached, organizations have the tools and processes to recover trusted data and limit the operational consequences. For enterprise IT teams, that makes recovery readiness an essential part of the cybersecurity conversation. Sponsored by Infinidat

technology.title: Space robot legend Voyager 1 is now more than 1 light-day away
technology.description: NASA's Voyager 1 probe is now more than one light-day from Earth – so distant that a radio signal takes 24 hours to reach it. The veteran spacecraft has spent almost 50 years getting there. Voyager 1 was launched on September 5, 1977, from Cape Canaveral in Florida. Planning for the mission began in the 1960s, while NASA was working feverishly to put a man on the Moon ahead of the Soviet Union. A rare alignment of the outer planets made a tour of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune possible. Voyager 2 eventually visited all four; Voyager 1's route prioritized Saturn's moon Titan, ruling out a subsequent encounter with Pluto. Voyager 1 completed a flyby of Jupiter in 1979, and passed Saturn and Titan in 1980. Its final imaging sequence in 1990 produced the solar system "Family Portrait," including the famous Pale Blue Dot image of Earth. The cameras were then switched off for good. Thirty-six years after those final pictures, Voyager 1 remains in contact with Earth, with two science instruments still operating: the magnetometer and plasma wave subsystem. Others have been shut down over the decades to conserve the dwindling power supplied by its radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs). Dr Garry Hunt, a member of Voyager's original imaging team, told The Register : "Voyager's real success is the way it used reliable equipment. Well-tested Mariner equipment, and special new things that had come about for it. "We had fault protection on board as well. If anything goes wrong, it automatically switches to a backup. So there was always a backup. There was always a safe mode. We had to have radiation protection on board … when we designed this, we didn't really know the magnetic environment around Jupiter, and to be told it was so strong, 1,000 times stronger than we anticipated, really threw everything up in the air, and so that had to be dealt with." Hunt paid tribute to the succession of project managers and engineers who have kept the probe running over the years. "I think this was a really wonderful example of project management, of clever management of engineering, and interesting science coming out of it, which has made history books and gone to be a catalyst for other things in the future," he said. Voyager 1 may now take two days to answer a call from Earth. After almost 50 years, the remarkable thing is that it still answers at all. ®

technology.title: StubHub International warns customer data may have left the venue
technology.description: Ticket resale giant StubHub International has warned customers that a recent breach may have exposed their personal information to cybercriminals. The company said it detected "unauthorized access to certain systems" on its platform between late October and early November. Customer notification emails seen by The Register list potentially affected information including names, email addresses, phone numbers, and country or regional settings. StubHub International, operated by Ticketbis S.L., apologized for the intrusion and offered the usual promise to implement security enhancements after the fact. The company said it had addressed "certain vulnerabilities" while containing the incident and was continuing to monitor for suspicious activity. Outside cybersecurity experts are assisting with the ongoing investigation. The company warned that any exposed information could be used to make subsequent scams more convincing. "To date, we have found no evidence of unauthorised access to account passwords , banking information or payment card details," the email stated. "We also have no evidence that the compromised information has been used fraudulently. "However, there is a risk that third parties could use this information to attempt fraud, identity theft or phishing through emails, messages or calls that appear to come from StubHub International or other trusted organizations." The Register contacted StubHub International for more information, such as how many customers were affected, but it did not respond. Digital Fuel Capital bought StubHub International from Viagogo in 2021 after the UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) required the international business to be sold to address competition concerns. In June, the CMA fined Ticketbis £889,200 and ordered refunds exceeding £590,000 after finding that mandatory fees were omitted from upfront ticket prices. StubHub International also recently faced criticism for allowing a single ticket tout to advertise £1 million worth of U2 tickets, despite its stated opposition to ticket-buying bots. ®

technology.title: How The Verge is picking which Black Friday deals to share
technology.description: For the past month, we’ve been inundated with Black Friday deals, signaling what’s to come on the biggest shopping day of the year in the US. We routinely get dozens of press releases a day, coming from brands big and small that hope that we’ll publicize these offers. Of course, the companies would prefer that we don’t do any research on these deals to see if they’re actually good, and most don’t provide any of the necessary context we’re looking for when vetting them. Most indicators of a good deal are confusing — not just for us, but for anyone who’s shopping. Groundwork Collaborative recently published its findings about the unclear manner in which Amazon displays deals. Its researchers tracked a selection of products ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday in 2024 and 2025, and they claim that nearly one in three products advertised as deals on Amazon didn’t offer savings during the actual shopping events. The investigation also found that nearly a tenth of the deals it examined were more expensive during the sales events than on some days in the month leading up to them. Something we commonly see on Amazon and attempt to correct for in our coverage are good deals with inflated discount claims. As in, the original retail amount (the “list” price) is sometimes higher than the usual day-to-day price to make the savings seem more substantial. Sometimes, the manufacturer’s suggested retail price (MSRP) is what’s shown, though that’s not always the case. In a recent statement to investigative journalist Ronan Farrow , an unattributed Amazon spokesperson shared that its “List Price” can also be aggregated from the past 90 to 180 days of prices, not the past 30 days as Groundwork Collaborative’s research states, and is based on prices from Amazon itself and other competing retailers. However, in our experience, the confusing way pricing and discounts are communicated isn’t limited to Amazon. View this post on Instagram The group’s findings show how easy it is to distrust the prices you see, especially online, where dynamic pricing sometimes comes into play. Regardless of retailer practices, we understand the importance of curating what you see on The Verge with care. Vetting deals for coverage consideration is a big, albeit invisible, part of our jobs, even outside of big shopping events. Most of what we’re pitched day to day, or what we see in our respective feeds, never hits the site because it doesn’t meet our standards. Even when the deal is for a product we’ve tested and really enjoy — our north star for what to cover on the deals front — that alone doesn’t guarantee coverage. We often skip covering deals that aren’t as good as a retailer or brand made them seem. Or maybe the deal is good, but it returns every week, lasts only a few hours, or it’s available only with a premium membership. technology.title: Business as usual, but Huang ain't coming back, says Nvidia
technology.description: Nvidia's board says it has no plans to bring Jensen Huang back as the GPU giant reports quarterly revenue more than double that of a year ago. The AI infrastructure leviathan had some reassuring to do after its leather-jacketed rockstar leader left under a cloud last week. Huang had been central to its rise as the dominant supplier of AI compute. Newly appointed board chair Harvey Jones ruled out an imminent comeback, saying: "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Jones said the board was addressing the fallout and strengthening oversight, pointing to the creation of a committee to scrutinize the firm's security policies and export compliance. Nvidia has also retained the services of talent spotters Heidrick & Struggles to help find a new leader, according to Jones. Interim CEO and chief financial officer Colette Kress struck an upbeat tone on the company's Q3 earnings call. The results gave her plenty to work with : revenue rose 103 percent to $115.8 billion, while operating income climbed 115 percent to $77.5 billion. "We're addressing strong demand for compute across a diverse and expansive set of end customers, including hyperscalers, frontier labs, AI natives, enterprises, and governments," Kress said. She raised Nvidia's outlook for fiscal 2028, saying that the firm now expects revenue to grow approximately 75 percent year-on-year. Analysts immediately questioned this, asking what gave Kress the confidence to raise the outlook, given all the uncertainty surrounding the future direction of the company. Kress cited growing demand and additional supply as reasons for lifting the fiscal 2028 growth forecast from 70 to 75 percent. When asked about the financing deals that Nvidia provides for some of its customers, Kress appeared to hint that some things might change. "Our neoclouds have been so instrumental in terms of both supporting enterprises and supporting many of the different countries around the world, particularly on the sovereign perspective. And we continue to be working with them," she stated. But she added: "I think we would look at this and take a very strong look in terms of the types of companies that we would want to help in terms of the financing, as a lot of things have changed over this last quarter... but we do have some very, very strong existing customers that we will be continuing to work with." Kress also said that Nvidia's rack-scale Rubin platform had generated nearly $20 billion in revenue in its first quarter of production shipments. She said the firm expects the major frontier AI labs to account for approximately 15 percent of its Data Center revenue this year. Kress said that Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed products based on its Hopper silicon to China, as scrutiny grows over Beijing's access to advanced AI technology, and so its future guidance does not count on any Hopper revenue from there. technology.title: Windows Server 2028 won't be compatible by default
technology.description: Microsoft has pushed Windows Server 2028 into public preview, with an eye on beefed-up security, new infrastructure support, and the inevitable nod to AI. Neil Hinnant, a director on the Windows Server team, talked up the security tweaks. There's a hardened Server Core configuration by default and a new security baseline. "Trusted Launch extends protection to virtual machines," he wrote . "Confidential VM support begins a journey to support integrity-protected runtimes on supported CVM hardware." Server Core will therefore arrive locked down by default – good news for security, potentially less so for administrators whose existing configurations depend on more permissive settings. "For years, Windows Server shipped compatible by default," wrote Senior Product Manager Christina Curlette. "Making the server secure was up to you, usually by applying the Security Baseline or your own hardening scripts after setup." With Windows Server 2028 (and starting from Windows Server Insider Preview build 29706), Server Core will be installed hardened. "Hundreds of security settings are on from first boot," Curlette wrote. "Because the defaults are now locked down, some things that worked on Windows Server 2025 may not work on Windows Server 2028 without changes. This includes older protocols, legacy authentication, and some management tools and scripts." For a company obsessed with backward compatibility, this is quite the step. Welcome though the hardening is, administrators will need to test carefully: working on Windows Server 2025 won't guarantee a smooth ride in the brave new world. AI gets a role on both sides of the security fence: helping uncover vulnerabilities and giving Microsoft another reason to sell servers. Windows Server 2028 is being pitched for running models locally, with support for accelerators such as AMD's Instinct MI350P. Not every server is destined to babysit a model, however, and the storage changes may be more immediately useful to enterprise administrators. Windows Server 2028 will enable native NVMe storage by default, along with NVMe over TCP and RDMA. Booting from ReFS is also planned, adding another item to the storage upgrade list. Intune management for Windows Server has also entered preview. Azure Arc, with its cloud-native management workflows, is obviously still around, while Intune brings a more familiar management interface for administrators already using it for endpoints. Hinnant acknowledged that this was a "major release," and it looks like the security hardening alone will require a good deal of thought from administrators before organizations adopt the eventual production release. Esben Dochy, Principal Technical Evangelist for SecOps at Lansweeper, told The Register that Microsoft had indicated that the hardened security only applied to new installations. technology.title: Police arrest 15 over £1.5M 'we'll recover your losses' scam targeting elderly
technology.description: Fifteen people have been arrested over an alleged scam that squeezed more money from investment fraud victims by offering to help recover their losses. City of London Police searched 17 London addresses on November 11 and apprehended 14 men and one woman. All have since been released on bail. Investigators say the suspected fraudsters posed as regulators to persuade previous victims that compensation was available. Reports submitted through the UK's Report Fraud service helped investigators trace the compensation pitch to around 3,000 recipients since October 2025. Most victims were elderly, police said. The offers arrived by letter and email, promising redress for earlier investment losses. City of London Police said the victims were initially targeted by a range of investment scams related to art, carbon credits, land, whisky, wine, and pensions, and that some took place more than a decade prior to their re-victimization. Targets were directed to a company that demanded a holding fee before supposedly reclaiming their money. Police say those who paid were left further out of pocket. "Today's action sends a clear message to those who target vulnerable people for financial gain: you will be pursued and will face robust action," said Nik Adams, deputy commissioner at the City of London Police. "Behind every fraud report is a real person whose trust has been damaged, and in some cases, whose life savings have been stolen. We know the impact of these crimes can be devastating. "This case highlights the importance of reporting fraud through the Report Fraud service. Information provided by victims helped investigators link reports together, uncover the wider conspiracy, and identify those involved. It is a powerful reminder that every report counts and can play a vital role in bringing offenders to justice." The investigation also extends beyond London, with police identifying locations linked to the case in Kent and Hertfordshire. The searches resulted in officers seizing cash, drugs, and other high-value items, including a watch worth around £230,000, with the total haul valued at more than £2 million. Police put losses identified so far at £1.5 million and expect that figure to rise as the investigation continues. Knowing the details of an earlier scam doesn't make a caller trustworthy, police warned. That information can be used to sell victims a second fraud. Report Fraud has also highlighted substantial losses in other scams affecting older people. Fraudsters exploiting positions of trust stole a reported £93.8 million during 2025/26. People aged 70 and over lost more than £51 million, with relatives, friends, carers, and others entrusted with their finances among the perpetrators. Report Fraud received 3,812 reports in this category. technology.title: ULA says Vulcan lacked the oomph to get Amazon satellites to orbit
technology.description: United Launch Alliance (ULA) says poor booster performance appears to have doomed Sunday's Vulcan mission, which lost an Amazon Leo satellite payload on the rocket's return to flight. ULA's initial assessment points to trouble almost immediately. "Early indications are that just after liftoff the launch vehicle experienced low booster performance," it said. As a result, stage separation occurred at too low an altitude, and the rocket was not traveling fast enough for the payload to reach orbit. The second stage appeared to perform well, with its RL10 engines operating as planned, but that wasn't enough to make up for the shortfall, and the mission failed . ULA lost telemetry approximately ten minutes into flight. An investigation is underway, led by ULA and overseen by the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), which had to activate two Debris Response Areas where debris was falling. The agency directs aircraft to leave these areas, and others are prevented from entering. Previous flights had been blighted by problems with the solid rocket boosters , designed to give the rocket a kick at launch. Those issues prompted a stand-down while investigators examined the cause. This time, ULA said: "All indications are that the solid rocket booster performance was nominal, following nozzle improvements implemented for this launch." Attention therefore turns to Vulcan's liquid-fueled core stage, powered by two Blue Origin BE-4 engines, though that does not establish an engine fault. Fuel delivery or another first-stage system could also be responsible, and the investigation is ongoing. The BE-4 also powers Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, which exploded on the launchpad during a ground test in May. In August, Blue Origin boss Dave Limp said that the issue originated at the main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines. Modifications were made to deal with the problem. The upper stage's apparently normal performance may offer some reassurance to NASA, although the investigation remains at an early stage. The agency dropped the delayed Exploration Upper Stage earlier this year and is pursuing a stretched Centaur V alongside its existing interim cryogenic propulsion stage as options for Artemis IV. NASA is targeting Artemis IV for early 2028 and Artemis V for later that year. ULA said: "We truly understand the impact this has on our customers and are committed to returning to flight as safely and quickly as we can." The failure also dents ULA's otherwise impressive launch record. A predecessor of Vulcan, the Atlas V, has a 100 percent success record for payloads reaching orbit. However, it uses Russian RD-180 engines, a dependency the US wishes to remove . ®

technology.title: UK.gov JV gets £178M Home Office hosting deal. Without competition
technology.description: The Home Office has awarded a contract worth £178 million to a public-private hosting services joint venture - without competition - to support critical national infrastructure. According to a notice published last week , Crown Hosting Data Centres (CHDC) won the seven-year contract to support "essential national infrastructure underpinning the Home Office's most critical systems, including border security, the Police National Computer (PNC), and core intelligence environments." CHDC is a joint venture between the Cabinet Office, which owns 25 percent, and Ark Data Centres Ltd, which owns the rest. It was set up in 2015 for the express purpose of providing hosting services for the government. The award was made through an existing framework agreement, set up in February 2022, awarded to CHDC without competition via a Voluntary Ex-Ante Transparency Notice . The service is set to support Critical National Infrastructure, although the notice does not reveal specific services requested. Mention of continued support for the Police National Computer may raise eyebrows. The Home Office is managing the transition of the aging legacy system to the Law Enforcement Data Service (LEDS) under the National Law Enforcement Data Program (NLEDP). A notice in December 2024 said that the Home Office was "focused on the development and adoption of LEDS products to replace existing PNC capability across all police forces and other non-policing PNC consumers, enabling the retirement by March 2026 (the point at which PNC support will expire)." The government had previously set a target of decommissioning the PNC in 2022. The Register has asked the Home Office to clarify why Crown Hosting support is necessary beyond this date. The PNC – which is based on mainframe technology dating from the 1970s – was at the center of a scandal in 2021 when a technology failure led to the loss of 413,000 records of evidence . The incident, which left then Prime Minister Boris Johnson floundering in Parliament, was the result of a scripting error in code designed to weed out records to be deleted from the PNC, a system running on a Fujitsu BS2000/OSD SE700-30 mainframe-based at a datacenter in Hendon, London. If you had been spying on me playing this game over the past few weeks you may well have caught me robbing banks, shooting up a weed farm or tearing along the highway at sunset blaring Bad Bunny on the in-game radio, but you might equally have caught me doing squats at the gym, shopping, assembling a coffee table or walking along the beach eating ice-cream. (Image credit: Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Acknowledgment: PIs: G. Narayan & T. Murphey (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign) Image processing: M. Zamani & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)) A new supernova has been spotted exploding in the spiral galaxy NGC 1433, about 50 million light-years from Earth. What is it? Researchers have discovered a new supernova called SN 2026ahvu. A Type Ia supernova, this event took place in a system with two stars orbiting one another (also known as a binary system), in which typically one star is an exploding white dwarf . During most type Ia supernovae, the white dwarf pulls material away from the other star until enough accumulates on its surface to create an explosion. Finding galaxies where stellar explosions are taking place isn't a rarity. However, this supernova is unique in how early it was captured. If the supernova were starting to dim, researchers might infer that the event was ending. However, according to details shared when it was first spotted, as well as later observations, this supernova was discovered while getting brighter. This indicates that the supernova was likely caught early in the process of exploding, providing researchers with a unique opportunity to observe the event as it is taking place. By exploring observations of the galaxy before, during and (in the future) after the supernova event, researchers can investigate this type Ia supernova and how it affected the system in which it took place. Why is it incredible? Scientists made this discovery using ATLAS, or the Asteroid Terrestrial-impact System, which is a robotic astronomical survey made up of telescopes across both hemispheres. ATLAS is designed to spot incoming near-Earth objects like asteroids before they can reach Earth. It's essentially an asteroid impact early warning system. But just because that's what the system is designed for doesn't mean that's all it can do. The system can also spot other objects moving through space and, in this instance, it was able to capture observations of this supernova. Following its initial discovery, other observations of the supernova were made using NOIRLab's Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and Gemini South telescope.

science.title: India's SatLeo Labs wants to build a 'thermometer for Earth' in space
science.description:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

AHMEDABAD, India — As climate disasters grow more frequent and severe, a young Indian space-tech startup is betting it can help the world act sooner by reading Earth's temperature from orbit in near-real time. SatLeo Labs, based here in western India, is building what it calls a " thermometer for Earth " in space. It plans to achieve its roadmap to deliver frequent, near-real-time thermal data through Pyro, a planned constellation of 15 microsatellites that will circle the planet in low Earth orbit by early 2030, if all goes to plan. Equipped with thermal sensors and onboard artificial intelligence , the satellites will measure the heat radiating from Earth's surface at a resolution finer than 10 meters (33 feet), which is sharp enough to map heat variations down to street level, the company says. "It's going to be that precise," SatLeo Labs co-founder Urmil Bakhai told Space.com in a recent interview. That level of detail, he said, helps distinguish temperatures across a single city and pinpoint urban hot spots, allowing governments and policymakers to plan targeted interventions and more heat-resilient city designs. The company is also targeting agriculture, and for good reason: Research suggests that thermal data can directly reveal water stress on crops days before leaves wilt, discolor or show other visible damage, unlike visible-light satellite imagery. Other uses the company is eyeing include spotting forest fires early, tracking industrial emissions and, on the defense side, detecting sudden temperature spikes from missile launches . Down the road, the team also envisions hyper-local uses. Near the top of its list are live heat maps built into navigation apps that could help gig-economy workers in India. These folks, who often ride motorcycles, could use the data to pick cooler routes during heat waves, said Bakhai. "We are in space, but we're solving problems on Earth ," said Shravan Bhati, SatLeo's co-founder and CEO. First, however, the company has to prove that its homegrown hardware works in space. On Oct. 1, SatLeo launched its first technology demonstrator, TAPAS-1, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket as part of the Transporter-18 rideshare mission. Short for "Thermal Access Platform for Analytics & Solutions," TAPAS-1 is India's first commercial thermal payload in orbit and the first of SatLeo's three planned test payloads meant to validate its technology. Once complete, the 15-satellite Pyro fleet will scan all of the world's land surface at least twice a day, Bakhai said. science.title: 1 light-day from Earth! NASA's Voyager 1 probe hits huge milestone in interstellar space
science.description: null NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is now one light-day from Earth — so far away that it takes signals a full 24 hours to reach the probe. Voyager 1 launched on Sept. 5, 1977, just a couple of weeks after Voyager 2 lifted off. But Voyager 1 launched on a faster trajectory than its twin and has just become the first spacecraft to ever reach one light-day away, which is equivalent to about 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), or the distance that one light particle travels in 24 hours. The milestone — which Voyager 1 hit today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) — shows the incredible ingenuity, technical ability and creativity from the teams at NASA that continue to innovate to keep this mission going nearly five decades later. "The Earth and Voyager are exactly 24 hours apart at the speed of light," Voyager Project Scientist Linda Spilker told Space.com. "It's a very special moment where Voyager 1 is about 16.1 billion miles away, and we're celebrating that moment because it's the first human-made object to actually reach one light-day distance." All things Voyager The two Voyager spacecraft have been on one serious ride since launching in 1977. And each of these twin probes has taken a unique and historic journey through our solar system and beyond. On Voyager 1's trip through our cosmic neighborhood, for example, it made countless groundbreaking observations of planets and moons that we had never before seen up close (or at all). The probe discovered a ring around Jupiter as well as the planet's moons Thebe and Metis. It also found five new moons and a new ring around Saturn. "Voyager 1 flew past the Jupiter system and took images of Jupiter's moon Io, and it actually discovered that Io is volcanically active. So, images that were taken showed these volcanoes that were actively erupting, and we learned that Io is actually the most volcanically active body in our solar system, which is just amazing," Cynthia Phillips, a project scientist for NASA's Europa Clipper mission, told Space.com about one of Voyager 1's many discoveries. science.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 18 – An… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Medium-Sized Solar Flare Explanation: What a flare for the chromatic ! Today’s image captures a piece of the Sun ’s chromosphere , the layer of the Sun ’s atmosphere above its surface where the temperature rises . Why would the Sun become hotter farther away from its core ? This is potentially due to energy from the swirling magnetic fields extending up through the Sun’s atmosphere. Those same magnetic fields can twist and snap , releasing light and energetic particles as a solar flare . The H-alpha filter used for today’s image captures light from energized hydrogen atoms as they travel off the Sun’s surface during a flare on May 14, 2025. This flare was classified as an M1 based on GOES observations , meaning it was moderately bright in X-rays . M-class flares can cause radio blackouts at Earth’s poles and minor radiation storms that can harm astronauts. They aren’t even the most powerful flares ! NASA, NOAA , and other agencies monitor the Sun to predict and identify such storms so we can protect humans on Earth and in space. science.title: NASA's Voyager 1 launched second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?
science.description: null Voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference? On Nov. 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal — so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky. But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer? It comes down to choices made for speed and science during the twin missions' nearly 50-year journey, specifically during the first bit when they were flying by planets. The result is Voyager 1 is zooming out at a speed of 3.5 Earth-sun distances (astronomical units a year), while Voyager 2 has a more stately speed of 3.1 Earth-sun distances, according to NASA . Need for speed The original aim of both the spacecraft, which launched about two weeks apart in 1977 with Voyager 2 going first, was to look at Jupiter and Saturn. If funding persisted, which it did, the hope was to bring Voyager 2 past Uranus and Neptune, taking advantage of a rare planetary alignment. Voyager 1, by contrast, made a turn at Saturn to look at the planet's rings and the prebiotic (pre-life-chemistry) moon of Titan , before flying outside the plane of the solar system. NASA had a range of trajectory options to consider when launching the spacecraft, and elected to bring Voyager 1 at a faster trajectory — as illustrated in this video by Britannica, where you can quickly see the spacecraft overtaking Voyager 2 on its way to Jupiter even though Voyager 1. Voyager 1 arrived at Jupiter on March 5, 1979 while Voyager 2 got there four months later on July 9. The trajectories of Voyager 1 and 2 through the outer solar system. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Each of the spacecraft then performed a "gravity assist"—a sort of slingshot around the planet in which they took a tiny bit of momentum from Jupiter to gain speed as the spacecraft flew to Saturn. This technique is used constantly, such as recently when the ESCAPADE Mars mission flew two spacecraft by Earth on the way to the Red Planet, as it allows spacecraft to gain speed while saving on fuel.
